# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage` and `internal/ui/datatable` |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line), tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost`, from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed

the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an

runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI

# DEVDESK-151 (A-13) — `:agent-usage`: activity column + Est. cost colouring

Model: DEVDESK-150 (#342, netdiag ports, new column) and DEVDESK-149 (templates, value-receiver view).
Package: `internal/ui/agentusageview` (value receivers: `func (m Model)`).

## Blocking question (Q1) — the 80-column layout

The new column costs 4 cells (2 + padding 2). Every non-yielding threshold moves +4:
State 63→67, Tools 70→74, **Duration 80→84**, Model 94→98, Breakdown 106→110, In 114→118,
Cache read 126→130, Est. cost 138→142, Cache write 151→155 (to be measured, not assumed).
Consequence: at 80 columns Duration disappears, which breaks DEVDESK-46 criterion 1
(`TestEveryAgentLineShowsStateToolsAndDurationAt80Columns`, `TestEstCostLayoutAtEachWidth` row 80).

- A. Accept it: at 80 → dot, Agent, ID, State, Tools, Out, Total, Share. Duration lost; the state is shown twice (dot + State).
- B. (recommended) Move the State column right of Duration (Agent, ID, Est. cost, Tools, Duration, State, Model, …).
  Drop order becomes …, Model, State, Duration, Tools: at 80 → dot, Agent, ID, Tools, Duration, Out, Total, Share.
  The dot carries the state (the story's own hypothesis: the dot matters on a narrow terminal, it repeats State on a wide one).
  State text column is kept (criterion 4). Cost: column order changes vs ux.md §3.4 mockup (120 cols).
- C. Keep everything and narrow something else (no candidate: Duration's MinWidth is its title).

## Hypotheses (prudent defaults, flag in PR)
- H1 Cost share denominator = sum of `Priced` estimates of **all** agents of the session (not the filter, not Billed).
  Unpriced/NoTokens agents excluded. "≥2 priced agents" = count of `Status == Priced`. Denominator ≤ 0 → no colour.
- H2 Footer sentences (ux.md §1.2 structure, times via `theme.TimeAgo`, Rule 127):
  running `Agent running — last transcript line <TimeAgo>`; idle `Agent idle — last transcript line <TimeAgo>`;
  done `Agent done — ran <formatDuration>` (just `Agent done` when no timestamp);
  unknown `Agent state unknown — transcript has no end marker` (sub-agent) / `Agent state unknown — updates are paused` (orchestrator).
- H3 Detail only on the Agents tab with a selected row; Breakdown tab and sessions level unchanged.
- H4 Blink only for a running row among `agentTable.Visible()`, level agents, tab Agents.
- H5 Risk, not a blocker: in a typical session the orchestrator holds ≥75 % of the cost, so it will often be orange/red (D6, user's call).

## Step 1 — state → indicator, cost share (pure)  [S]
Files: `status.go`, `agents.go`, `cost.go`; tests `status_test.go`, `cost_test.go`.
- `func (s runState) indicator() indicator.State` : running→Running, idle→Suspended, done→Done, unknown→Unknown.
- `agentRow` gains `costPct float64` and `costRanked bool`, set once in `agentRows` (never in a Cell):
  `func costShares(es []pricing.Estimate) (pct []float64, ranked bool)`.
- Tests: table on the 4 states (4 distinct `indicator.Glyph(…, true)`, none `●` except running; `○` off phase only for running);
  costShares: 0 priced → ranked=false; 1 priced → false; 2 priced 80/20 → true, [80,20]; unpriced agent excluded from the denominator;
  all priced at $0 → false; negative/NaN never panics.
Done when: `go test ./internal/ui/agentusageview/ -run 'State|CostShare'` green.

## Step 2 — activity column + layout recalibration  [M]  (depends on 1; decision Q1)
Files: `agents.go` (`agentColumns`: column 0 = `datatable.IndicatorColumn(func(r agentRow) indicator.State { return r.state.indicator() }, nil, nil)`;
if Q1=B move `stateColumn()` after `durationColumn()`), `help.go` (narrow-terminal drop-order sentence),
`docs/architecture/agent-usage.md` (columns table, "Column order and width", every threshold, the 80/60 layouts, Breakdown "Visible from …").
Tests to update/write (measure each switch width, do not add 4 blindly):
- `cost_test.go` `TestEstCostLayoutAtEachWidth` + its comment; `breakdown_column_test.go` threshold table (~l.217-234, `106` loop l.299);
  `activity_columns_test.go` 80/60 tests; `yield_test.go`; `agents_level_test.go` `TestTwoCodersStayDistinctOnANarrowTerminal` must still pass.
- New: `header()` helper must ignore the untitled column; column 0 untitled, `SizingFixed`, `IconColumnWidth`, no Less/Search;
  at 60 cols State absent and each row starts with its glyph (◐ for idle, ◉ done, ◌ unknown, ● running);
  Rule 116 at 50..230 via `RenderedWidth()`, also with `runewidth.EastAsianWidth = true`.
Done when: `go test ./internal/ui/agentusageview/...` green.

## Step 3 — blink (router frame)  [S]  (depends on 2)
Files: new `internal/ui/agentusageview/activity.go`, `update.go`.
- `func (m Model) ActivityTables() map[string]datatable.ActivityTable { return map[string]datatable.ActivityTable{"agent-usage/agents": &m.agentTable} }`
- `func (m Model) WantsBlink() bool` — H4.
- `update.go`: `case jobs.FrameMsg: m.agentTable.SetBlinkPhase(msg.Blink); return m, nil`.
Tests (package): WantsBlink true with a running agent on Agents tab; false on Breakdown tab, at sessions level, with only idle/done/unknown,
when the running row is filtered out; FrameMsg{Blink:false} → row shows `○`, true → `●`;
handlePollTick / applyRead never return an animation tick (`grep tea.Tick` stays empty; guard covers it).
New `internal/app/agent_usage_activity_test.go`: transcript on disk (pattern `TestAgentUsageTrailSitsOnTheTopBorder`, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR,
line with a fresh `timestamp`), open the session, `held.WantsBlink()` true, `jobs.FrameMsg` on/off flips the glyph (model: `netdiag_activity_test.go`);
with `a.motionStatic = true`, `ensureTick()` returns nil.
Done when: `go test ./internal/ui/agentusageview/... ./internal/app -run 'AgentUsage|Animation|Activity'` and `mise run test-race` on `internal/app` green.

## Step 4 — footer detail + help legend  [S]  (depends on 2; parallel with 3 if same branch rebased)
Files: `view.go` (`agentsStatus`), new `func (m Model) agentDetail() sharedcomponents.RowDetail` in `activity.go`, `help.go`.
- `st := …; st.Detail = m.agentDetail()` like `PortsModel.statusLine`; detail via
  `components.DescribeRow(components.RowQuery{Observed: r.state.indicator(), ObservedText: sentence}).Detail` (H2, H3).
- `help.go`: add `indicator.Legend(indicator.AgentsLegend...)` section (the extension already exists in `indicator/legend.go`);
  State paragraph says the dot repeats it.
Tests: each state → footer starts with its glyph + sentence (ansi-stripped); error/loading still win (Level error kept);
no detail on Breakdown tab; help has "Activity indicator" section with `◐ idle (no activity for 5 min)`; `GetShortcuts()` unchanged (Rule 130).

## Step 5 — Est. cost colouring  [S]  (depends on 1; parallel with 3/4)
File: `cost.go` `costColumn().Style`:
`!Priced → theme.DimStyle`; `!r.costRanked || r.costPct < theme.LoadWarnPercent → lipgloss.NewStyle()`;
else `theme.LoadTextStyle(r.costPct)`. **Never call LoadTextStyle below 75: it returns green (ColorOK).**
Tests: 80/20 → orchestrator cell Style fg = ColorSeverityMedium, 95/5 → ColorSeverityCritical, 60/40 → no fg, one priced agent at 100 % → no fg,
`-` dim; Cell text unchanged (plain, Rule 122); Style stays when the row is selected (normal selection); help "Costs" section mentions the colours.
Docs: agent-usage.md "Est. cost" paragraph (D6 exception, not an activity colour).

## Step 6 — guard + docs  [S]  (last, after 2-5)
- `internal/app/activity_guard_test.go`: `migratedTables[command.ViewAgentUsage] = {"agent-usage/agents"}`; drop the A-13 pendingTables entry;
  `maxPendingTables` 6→5; `migratedSources[command.ViewAgentUsage] = {"ui/agentusageview/"}` (no tea.Tick in the package: pollTickCmd sleeps in a Cmd);
  `migratedFooterSeeds[command.ViewAgentUsage] = seedAgentUsageFooter` (transcript on disk, returns `indicator.Running`; run Cmds but never the 2 s poll Cmd).
- `animation_guard_test.go`: nothing to remove (no declared chain for agent-usage).
- Docs same commit: `app-shell.md` l.993 (6 to 5 with `agent-usage/agents`, DEVDESK-151), `agent-usage.md` (columns, WantsBlink, footer, colour),
  `ui-components.md` if it lists the migrated views, `stories.md` A-13 status, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` overview line for :agent-usage (dot column, cost colour).
Done when: `go test ./internal/app -run 'Activity|Animation|AgentUsage'`, `mise run check`, `mise run test-race` green.

## Blocking question (Q1) — the 80-column layout

The new column costs 4 cells (2 + padding 2). Every non-yielding threshold moves +4:
State 63→67, Tools 70→74, **Duration 80→84**, Model 94→98, Breakdown 106→110, In 114→118,
Cache read 126→130, Est. cost 138→142, Cache write 151→155 (to be measured, not assumed).
Consequence: at 80 columns Duration disappears, which breaks DEVDESK-46 criterion 1
(`TestEveryAgentLineShowsStateToolsAndDurationAt80Columns`, `TestEstCostLayoutAtEachWidth` row 80).

- A. Accept it: at 80 → dot, Agent, ID, State, Tools, Out, Total, Share. Duration lost; the state is shown twice (dot + State).
- B. (recommended) Move the State column right of Duration (Agent, ID, Est. cost, Tools, Duration, State, Model, …).
  Drop order becomes …, Model, State, Duration, Tools: at 80 → dot, Agent, ID, Tools, Duration, Out, Total, Share.
  The dot carries the state (the story's own hypothesis: the dot matters on a narrow terminal, it repeats State on a wide one).

- H2 Footer sentences (ux.md §1.2 structure, times via `theme.TimeAgo`, Rule 127):
  running `Agent running — last transcript line <TimeAgo>`; idle `Agent idle — last transcript line <TimeAgo>`;
  done `Agent done — ran <formatDuration>` (just `Agent done` when no timestamp);
  unknown `Agent state unknown — transcript has no end marker` (sub-agent) / `Agent state unknown — updates are paused` (orchestrator).
- H3 Detail only on the Agents tab with a selected row; Breakdown tab and sessions level unchanged.
- H4 Blink only for a running row among `agentTable.Visible()`, level agents, tab Agents.
- H5 Risk, not a blocker: in a typical session the orchestrator holds ≥75 % of the cost, so it will often be orange/red (D6, user's call).

Tu rédiges la documentation destinée aux lecteurs du produit (utilisateurs et développeurs).

## Méthode

1. Identifie le lecteur et ce qu'il veut accomplir.
2. Vérifie chaque commande, chemin et exemple dans le code ou en l'exécutant ;
   n'invente rien.

Phrases courtes, voix active, un exemple exécutable par concept. Reprends la langue
et le ton de la documentation déjà présente dans le projet.

Décisions et `CLAUDE.md` → `archivist`. Changelog et notes de version → `devops`.

Si une information qui change le résultat manque ou est ambiguë (public visé, comportement réel d'une commande, prérequis), ne la devine
pas : arrête-toi et rends tes questions en tête de ta sortie, sous **Questions
bloquantes**, chacune avec les options possibles et ta recommandation. L'orchestrateur

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. content.content:
`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or
`enter` opens the selected session's agents (DEVDESK-42, below).

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |

- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
  are dated, not wrong.
- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
  the model.

### Second level: the session's agents (DEVDESK-42)

`→`/`enter` on a session opens its agents; `←`/`esc` goes back to the list.
`agents.go` builds the table, `availability.go` decides what the keys allow.

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Agent | `orchestrator`, then each sub-agent's type behind `├─ ` / `└─ ` in tree order, bare when sorted (`unknown` when the meta file gave none). `/` matches the role only. |
| ID | the sub-agent's short ID (`shortAgentIDs`): the smallest common length >= 8 runes at which all IDs of the session differ, capped at each ID's own length. `-` for the orchestrator, `?` for a sub-agent with an empty ID. `/` matches the full ID here. Never dropped, so two agents of one type stay apart. |
| Model | the models the agent used, comma-separated; `-` (dim) when none. `Optional`. |
| Breakdown | the token mix as a 10-cell bar (DEVDESK-128): `Cell` is `theme.GaugeFill(10)` (plain text), `Spans` paints `agentRow.mix` with the four `theme.TokenStyle` roles in the order Input, Output, Cache write, Cache read; a dim `-` when the agent has no token. `mix`/`hasMix` are computed once in `agentRows` via `segmentCells`. Fixed width 10, `Optional`, no sort or search. The glyph is `app.gauge_glyph`'s (`theme.GaugeFill`); the bar has no track, so colour is the only thing that separates its parts (Rule 122, fifth declared exception). `apportion` (`breakdown_bar.go`) splits the 10 cells with the largest-remainder method on 128-bit-safe `math/big` integers: a category worth less than half a cell gets no cell of its own, leftover cells go to the largest part, ties go to the larger part then the lowest index. A bar therefore always fills its 10 cells when the agent has any token, and a small category can vanish: the exact figures are in the In/Out/Cache columns and in the Breakdown tab. Visible from 106 columns with short agent types (110 with `general-purpose`, 125 with a 30-character type). |
| In, Out, Cache read, Cache write, Total | token counts. On a narrow terminal the drop order is `Cache write`, `Est. cost`, `Cache read`, `In`, `Breakdown`, `Model`, `Duration`, `Tools`, `State`. `Out` and `Total` stay. |
| State | `running`, `idle`, `done` or `unknown` (DEVDESK-46, see "Agent state and activity"). Fixed width, `Optional`. `/` matches the label. |
| Tools | `Agent.ToolCalls`, compact like tokens; a dim `0`. Fixed, `Optional`. |
| Duration | `Agent.Duration()` (`formatDuration`): `45s`, `3m07s`, `1h05m`, `2d03h`, `>99d`, floored, at most 6 cells; a dim `-` when the transcript has no timestamp. Fixed, `Optional`. |
| Est. cost | the estimated cost in USD (DEVDESK-47), see "Est. cost" below. Fixed width 10, `Optional` and `DropFirst`. No sort. |
| Share | the agent's part of the session total (`Usage.Total().Total()`), see below. Fixed width. |

- **Share (`share.go`).** Tenths of a percent, floored, computed on 128 bits
  (`bits.Mul64`/`Div64`) so no product overflows; a part is clamped to
  `[0, total]`. The orchestrator absorbs the rounding residue, so the column
  sums to `100.0%`; the residue is clamped at 0 when saturated totals overshoot.
  With no orchestrator row nothing is absorbed. A session with no tokens gives
  `noShare` and the cell shows a dim `-`. Rendered as `12.3%`.
- **Column order and width.** Agent, ID, Est. cost, State, Tools, Duration, Model, Breakdown, In, Out,
  Cache read, Cache write, Total, Share. With three sub-agents, 100 columns show
  Agent, ID, State, Tools, Duration, Model, Out, Total, Share; 80 columns drop
  Model as well; 60 columns drop Duration, Tools and State and show the five

`status.go` derives the State column. The package describes what the transcripts
say; what counts as "idle" is a display policy that depends on the view's clock,
so it lives here, not in `internal/agentusage`. `agentStates` is pure: the clock
is a parameter (`statusClock{now, alive}`).

- **`alive`** means the poll chain is live: `!Settled(at, quietPeriod)`. There is
  no other source (no process probe, no session registry): it also works for a
  transcript copied from elsewhere.
- **`quiet`** means `now - LastActivity > idleAfter` (5 min), **strictly**: at
  exactly 5 min an agent is still running. No timestamp, or a timestamp in the
  future (clock skew), is never quiet.
- **`now` is `usageDeltaMsg.at`**, the moment the read finished, not the wall
  clock at render time, so the same answer gives the same states on every frame.

| Agent | Condition | State |
|---|---|---|
| sub-agent | meta `finished: true` | `done` |
| sub-agent | meta `finished: false` | `running`, or `idle` when quiet, whether or not the session is alive |
| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session alive | `running` / `idle` as above |
| sub-agent | no `finished` key, session not alive | `unknown` |
| orchestrator | session alive | `running`, or `idle` when quiet **and no sub-agent is `running`** |
| orchestrator | session not alive | `unknown` |

The orchestrator is **never `done`**: Claude Code writes no end marker for it. A
foreground `Agent` call leaves it silent for as long as the sub-agent runs, so it
is not idle while one runs; if every running sub-agent is itself idle, it is idle
too. Once updates pause it reads `unknown`, so a session waiting at the prompt for
more than 5 min shows `unknown` and `Updates › paused`. Colours (Rule 122): `idle`
in the MEDIUM orange, `unknown` dim, `running` and `done` in the text colour.

**The rows are rebuilt on every successful read, even an empty one** (`applyRead`
in `update.go`). An agent turns idle precisely because nothing arrives, so an
empty delta must still move the clock. `settled` is computed once and used for
both the clock and the decision to stop polling; while a `ctrl+r` full read is
pending the session counts as alive, so the header does not flash `paused`.
`withUsage` is `withRows` plus clearing the loading and error flags; population
is unchanged on an empty delta, so there is no `Remeasure` and the selection
stays on its agent. On `os.ErrNotExist`, `failRead` marks the clock not alive and
calls `withRows` (not `withUsage`), so the red footer stays. Opening or leaving a
session resets the clock.

A-09b, explorer A-10a / A-10b) when the two sets are disjoint, and an exempt
view is neither:

| List | Meaning |
